chunks: 'Ali narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, from his father, from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام:

Concerning three men who testified against a man for zina, Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: 'Where is the fourth?' He said: 'He is coming now.' So Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: 'Administer the hadd to them, for in the hudud there is no waiting even for an hour.'

key_terms.الرَّابِعُ: the fourth witness required to complete the legal testimony
key_terms.الزِّنَى: zina; unlawful sexual intercourse requiring strict evidentiary standards for legal establishment
key_terms.الْحُدُودِ: the fixed legal punishments ordained in sacred law
key_terms.حُدُّوهُمْ: apply the hadd punishment to them

ai.seo_question: What happens if only three witnesses testify in a zina accusation in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning testimony in a zina case, where three witnesses are insufficient and the absence of the required fourth witness leads to punishment for the accusers. It highlights the strict procedural standards in hudud and the necessity of immediate legal judgment once the deficiency in proof is established.
